title: Instrumentation Gambit — heuristics and dashboard deck notes (WIP)
body:
Status: draft — this is a working note for the Q4 instrumentation push and the companion dashboard deck we will present to SRE/Product/Platform next month.

Purpose:
- Define a minimal, tiered signal set we can reliably ship in a 6-week sprint that improves triage for latency regressions, cost spikes, and cache-warmth problems.
- Propose a tracing anchor model and sampling strategy that keeps trace volumes bounded while preserving high-value tails.
- Sketch dashboard prioritization for three personas: oncall SRE, engineering investigator, and product rollout owner.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce mean time to root cause for cold-cache latency incidents by 30% in Q1.
- Keep trace ingestion delta under +15% relative to baseline by applying adaptive sampling and microprobe scheduling.
- Surface the 95th/99th token-latency contributors on a single drilldown panel for faster cohorting.

Signal tiering (proposal):
- Tier 0 (must-have): request-level latency quantiles (TTF.start, TTF.first-token, TTF.last-token), error counts (per-model), request size, tenant id.
- Tier 1 (high value): kv-cache hit/miss tag, batching bucket id (small/medium/large), route model variant, region, container hotness.
- Tier 2 (experimental / sampled): per-op microspans (encoder, attention-kernel, kv-lookup), token-level generation latency histogram, GPU-utilization per shard.

Metric definitions (working):
- request_ttf_first_byte_ms: time from API gateway receive to first token byte emitted. aggregation: p50/p90/p95/p99, count, rate.
- request_ttf_last_token_ms: time from API gateway receive to final token. aggregation: p50/p90/p95/p99, count, rate.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: hits / (hits + misses) over 1m windows. taggable by model_family and tenant_weight.
- batching_effectiveness_index: (tokens_processed / batch_slots_used) per minute. tracks batching efficiency and queueing amplification.
- model_fanout_multiplier: number of model invocations per logical request. helps identify multi-model regressions.

Tracing anchors and span model (sketch):
- Root span: request:<request_id> with attributes: tenant, route, model_variant, input_length, priority.
- Child spans: routing.check, kv.lookup (idempotent, include hit/miss boolean), batch.join, model.invoke (attach batch_size, seq_len, quantization_profile), postprocess.render.
- Span tagging rules: use stable keys for span.name to allow aggregation; avoid embedding long user prompts in tags. If prompt hash is needed, use prompt_sha256:prefix.
- Correlate logs->traces by request_id and trace_id at ingress layer. ensure the gateway enriches requests with both ids.

Sampling strategy (practical):
- Baseline 0.5% uniform trace sampling for all requests.
- Severity-weighted upsampling: any request that hits p99 latency OR generates an error -> force-sample (100%).
- Session-affinity boosting: If a tenant has >1 forced-sampled request in 5m, sample 5% of their requests to capture context.
- Adaptive probe schedule: enable microprobe traces for 1% of requests during planned rollout windows; turn off outside windows.
- TTL and retention tiers: full traces for 7 days, condensed trace breadcrumbs (span anchors + metadata) for 30 days.

Dashboard prioritization (persona-driven):
- Oncall SRE (microdash): single landing panel that shows request rate, p95 TTF, kb-cache warmth (kv_cache_hit_ratio), incident count, and a ranked list of top-k tenants by p99. Quick links: click a tenant -> pre-populated investigation query and trace view.
- Engineering Investigator (investigation canvas): composite panel: latency heatmap by input_length x model_variant, trace-sampled waterfall viewer, batching distribution histogram, and cost-per-token time-series.
- Product/Rollout (rollout deck): change in perceived latency (p50/p90/p95) for cohort, regression flag if p95 increases >10% and error rate > baseline+0.1%.

Probe orchestration & experiment plan (timeline):
- Week 1: implement metric guards and p95/p99 calculation in ingestion pipeline; deploy kv_cache_ratio.
- Week 2: ship root/span naming changes and attach request_id at gateway. small canary (5% traffic).
- Week 3: enable severity-weighted sampling; run baseline trace-volume sim for 72h.
- Week 4: dashboard draft + microdash for oncall; dry-run alerting rules.
- Week 5: rollout to 25% customer traffic; monitor cost delta.
- Week 6: iterate based on ops feedback; final deck prep.

Quick SQL snippets (for dashboards / probe checks):
- Count high-cardinality tenants in last 24h:
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(distinct request_id) as requests FROM telemetry.requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '24h' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY requests DESC LIMIT 200;
- Approx kv warmth per tenant:
  SELECT tenant_id, SUM(kv_hits)::float / NULLIF(SUM(kv_hits+kv_misses),0) as kv_warmth FROM telemetry.kv_events WHERE ts > now() - interval '1h' GROUP BY tenant_id;

Operational heuristics / tradeoffs to note:
- Cardinality: tenant_id + model_variant + route is high-cardinality. prefer tag sampling or rollup keys for non-critical dashboards.
- Cost: token-level histograms are very expensive. only enable token histo for <1% of traffic and collapse into quantiles for dashboards.
- Privacy: ensure prompt hashes are used instead of raw prompt text in any telemetry storage; redact PII at ingress.

Open decisions / questions:
1) Retention tiers: is 7d full traces / 30d condensed acceptable to Legal? (ask security/compliance).
2) Do we want a "replay" path to rehydrate condensed breadcrumbs into a synthetic trace if needed? cost estimate needed.
3) How aggressive should session-affinity boosting be for enterprise tenants under dedicated/Dedicated customers?
4) Which existing dashboards should be deprecated to keep query budget neutral? (proposal: deprecate two low-value panels per new high-cost panel shipped).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: trace volume spike during rollout -> mitigation: kill-switch in ingestion and adaptive sampling applied at gate.
- Risk: operator overload from too many alerts -> mitigation: bundle similar symptoms into single incident with root-cause tags and reduce duplicate counts.

Next steps / owners:
- Liam Chen: finalize span naming conventions and push gateway enrichment change (PR in telemetry repo). target: Week 2.
- Aisha Patel: dashboard draft for microdash and oncall panel, add quick-links. target: Week 4.
- Mateo Alvarez: sampling sim and cost estimation. target: Week 3.
- Zoe Park: compliance check for retention/PII policy. target: Week 2.

References & links:
- Telemetry repo experiments: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/tree/main/experiments/instrumentation-gambit
- Confluence note: CONF-8421:Observability-instrumentation-gambit
- Slack thread: #observability (thread ts: 1709502000.000200)
- Related tickets: JIRA-OPS-1287, JIRA-OBS-1340

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep the deck under 12 slides. Start with user story: "Customer sees latency spike; SRE finds root cause in 6 minutes". Include a small sequence diagram of span flow through gateway->router->kv->model.
- Experiment idea: synthetic probe that replays 100 templated prompts across model variants to measure p95 drift hourly. Could live in probes-service.
- Avoid introducing new high-cardinality labels without a clear rollup plan.

That’s the working draft. Will convert key sections into the deck and the microdash JSON next.
